scenarioStory.history: Warehouse worker found with his right leg pinned from mid-shin down under a collapsed section of pallet racking after a forklift operation went wrong. Coworkers attempted to lift the rack manually without success before calling 911. Entrapment time is approximately 35 minutes and climbing while fire/rescue rigs airbags and cribbing. Patient is alert, in severe pain, denies loss of consciousness or head strike.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 45-year-old male pinned under collapsed pallet racking, alert and in severe pain, with an entrapment time already exceeding 30 minutes. Fire/rescue is on scene rigging equipment for extrication but has not yet released the pressure. → IV fluids and bicarb given before release: Crew establishes IV access and administers fluids, sodium bicarbonate, and analgesia while fire/rescue continues rigging for a controlled release, per the crush injury protocol's requirement that fluids precede release of the entrapping pressure. → Extrication coordinated after fluids given: Fire/rescue performs a controlled lift of the racking while the crew maintains fluid resuscitation and watches the cardiac monitor closely for signs of hyperkalemia as the crushed leg is released. → Stable release, no hyperkalemia signs: The patient remains hemodynamically stable after release with no EKG evidence of hyperkalemia. The crew continues fluid resuscitation and prepares for rapid transport to a trauma center.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Right lower leg pinned under collapsed pallet racking, severe pain

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 45-year-old male pinned under collapsed pallet racking, alert and in severe pain, with an entrapment time already exceeding 30 minutes. Fire/rescue is on scene rigging equipment for extrication but has not yet released the pressure.
relatedChecklist: Establish IV access (two large-bore lines preferred)
Attach cardiac monitor and obtain 12-lead EKG; watch for hyperkalemia changes
Administer 1,000 mL normal saline IV bolus before release (avoid lactated Ringer's)
Sodium bicarbonate 50 mEq IV over 5 min (90 kg × 1 mEq/kg = 90 mEq → capped at 50 mEq max)
Fentanyl 90 mcg IV (90 kg × 1 mcg/kg; max initial dose 100 mcg)

scenarioEvents.name: IV fluids and bicarb given before release
scenarioEvents.description: Crew establishes IV access and administers fluids, sodium bicarbonate, and analgesia while fire/rescue continues rigging for a controlled release, per the crush injury protocol's requirement that fluids precede release of the entrapping pressure.
relatedChecklist: Continuously monitor EKG for peaked T waves, widening QRS during and after release
Continue normal saline infusion through and after extrication

scenarioEvents.name: Extrication coordinated after fluids given
scenarioEvents.description: Fire/rescue performs a controlled lift of the racking while the crew maintains fluid resuscitation and watches the cardiac monitor closely for signs of hyperkalemia as the crushed leg is released.
relatedChecklist: Continue normal saline infusion at 500–1,000 mL/hr post-extrication
Rapid transport to a trauma center; reassess neurovascular status and pain en route

scenarioEvents.name: Stable release, no hyperkalemia signs
scenarioEvents.description: The patient remains hemodynamically stable after release with no EKG evidence of hyperkalemia. The crew continues fluid resuscitation and prepares for rapid transport to a trauma center.

scenarioEvents.name: Release attempted before fluids
scenarioEvents.description: Fire/rescue releases the racking before adequate IV fluids were given, producing an abrupt reperfusion event: sudden hypotension, tachycardia, and diaphoresis as unbuffered potassium and toxins wash into circulation.
relatedChecklist: Recognize reperfusion syndrome: sudden hypotension and arrhythmia risk after release without adequate fluids

scenarioEvents.name: Peaked T waves recognized post-release
scenarioEvents.description: The EKG develops peaked T waves and a widening QRS shortly after a properly fluid-resuscitated release, prompting immediate hyperkalemia treatment.
relatedChecklist: Calcium chloride 1 g IV over 5 min (ensure IV patency; do not exceed 1 mL/min)
Consider albuterol 5 mg nebulized for hyperkalemia; may repeat if no response
